blocks.why: Last normal night in your own bed before a month that goes sideways — bank it while it's free.
Afternoon nap before the 16:00Z report — GRU is a 13h40 duty that lands you at 02:10 local, so go in with sleep in the tank.
Straight to bed at the hotel around 03:15 local; blackout the room and take the seven hours while your body still thinks it's mid-morning at home.
Top-up before the 20:00Z report because you're about to fly another full night straight back to LHR.
Home about 10:35Z after an all-nighter — three and a half hours only, then get up so you can still sleep tonight.
Proper night at home to reset before the Chicago pairing starts.
Nap before the 16:00Z report — you won't be in a bed again until 22:00 Chicago time.
Bed at 22:30 local as soon as you're in the hotel; that's 04:30 body time so you'll drop straight off.
Short lunchtime nap on the day off to bridge a long gap — keep it under an hour so it doesn't rob tonight.
Early night, 20:30 to 06:00 local, ahead of the 08:45 local report — this one has to carry you until you're home past midnight UK time.
In the door about 01:10Z, so straight to bed — this is your only real sleep before tonight's westbound.
Non-negotiable nap before the 20:40Z report — the whole duty sits inside your window of circadian low and you land at 01:40 Chicago time.
Off duty at 02:10 local after a full night awake — take a long one, you have the whole day free afterwards.
Early to bed local time so you're rested for the 13:45Z report and the long day back to LHR.
Home just after 01:00Z — sleep it off, then get outside in daylight to start pulling the body clock back east.
First proper UK night after Chicago; it'll feel early but hold the line to get back on local time.
Insurance nap before the 12:00Z standby window in case they call you late in it for something long.
Standby released at 20:00Z with nothing on it — normal night, stay on local time.
Same insurance nap before the second standby day.
Ordinary night at home on a clear day.
Go down an hour early — sim reports 07:00Z, which means the alarm at 06:00 local and out the door by 06:05Z.
Short one after the sim to take the edge off, kept early enough not to spoil the night.
Start of the long block of days off — settle into a fixed 23:00/07:00 local pattern.
Days off — keep the same hours rather than drifting late, it's what makes the GRU trip survivable.
Days off — same window, hold it.
Days off — same window, hold it.
Days off — same window, hold it.
Days off — same window, hold it.
Full eight and a half before the GRU day sector — you'll be awake from 07:00Z until the hotel at about 00:15Z, so this is the whole day's fuel.
In the hotel by 21:15 local after a seventeen-hour day — sleep now, don't sit up.
Long afternoon anchor sleep, 12:00 to 18:30 local, because tomorrow's report is 00:40Z and you're flying the whole night home.
Two hours only after the 13:50Z landing — enough to be human for the evening, not enough to wreck the night.
Back onto UK nights straight away with three clear days before Los Angeles.
Day off — normal night, no lie-ins, you've got an early report coming.
Down at 22:30 local for the 07:45Z report — sleep before an early is always short, so start it early.
Ninety minutes on arrival at 14:30 local to take the edge off, then out into the afternoon light — don't let it become the night.
Bed at 21:30 local; you only need to come halfway onto LA time because Monday's report is 08:45 local.
Early-afternoon nap on the day off so you're not running on empty by the time tonight's main sleep comes round.
Nine and a half hours, 21:00 to 06:30 local, before an eleven-hour night crossing that finishes at 04:45Z — take everything you can get and use the bunk on top.
Home about 05:40Z with your body clock on LA time, so 07:00 to 13:00 local is the sleep you'll actually get.
In bed by 20:30 local for a 04:15 alarm — it's only lunchtime to your body, so blackout, no caffeine after mid-afternoon, and treat anything you get as a bonus.
If standby runs off at 13:00Z without a call, take an hour to pay back last night's short sleep.
Close the month out on a normal UK night.

conflicts.statement: The 22 Sep line carries '+1' on every field (report 00:40Z+1, STD 02:10Z+1, STA 13:50Z+1), which places the duty on 23 Sep — but 23 Sep is printed OFF and the header's 'Days Off: 16' counts it as a day off. I have planned it as a 23 Sep duty; 22 Sep is a GRU layover day.
options: Get crewing to reissue the line so the duty date and the OFF marker agree before you plan anything around 23 Sep
Confirm with ops whether PW344 is 02:10Z on 23 Sep as I've read it, and get it in writing
If it is genuinely intended as 22 Sep, refuse it on rest grounds — see the minimum-rest conflict on the same date
Assume 23 Sep for personal planning but do not commit to anything on 23 Sep until it's confirmed

conflicts.statement: Read literally as 22 Sep, PW344 reports at 00:40Z just 50 minutes after off-duty at 23:50Z on 21 Sep at GRU — that is not a rest period, it's a coffee break, and it cannot be what was intended.
options: Treat the literal reading as a printing error and work to the 23 Sep interpretation
Ask crewing to confirm the layover length at GRU in writing before you leave LHR on 21 Sep
If crewing insist on 22 Sep, decline on rest and let the operator resolve it

conflicts.statement: PW895 reports 20:40Z and runs to 07:10Z, sitting across 02:00–06:00 body time from end to end, on a body clock still set to London after only about 19 hours at home following a 00:15Z arrival the night before.
options: Protect the 15:00–17:30Z nap absolutely — no errands, phone off, room blacked out
Plan controlled rest in the cruise with the other pilot and brief it before top of climb
Save caffeine for the second half of the sector rather than using it early
If the nap doesn't happen, call it in before report rather than after

conflicts.statement: Two back-to-back 13h40 night duties around a GRU layover of only about 14h20, with off-duty at 02:40 local and report at 17:00 local — one sleep opportunity, taken at a body time that's already out of phase.
options: Ask the hotel for early check-in and a blackout room, and go straight up from the crew bus
Take the 13:30–15:00 local nap even if you don't feel you need it
Plan bunk rest on the return sector with the augmenting crew before departure
Flag the layover length to your fatigue reporting system whether or not it bites this time

conflicts.statement: Wake around 07:00Z for the 10:10Z report and you are not in the GRU hotel until about 00:15Z — roughly 17 hours 15 minutes awake, ending at 21:15 local in a station four hours behind you.
options: Sleep to 07:00Z rather than getting up early, even if it's a slow morning
Take a bunk slot in the second half of the cruise so the awake period is broken
Eat properly in the cruise rather than arriving hungry and wired
Do not plan anything in GRU that evening — bus, room, bed

conflicts.statement: Standby starts 05:00Z, which means a 04:15 local alarm and leaving home at 04:05Z, roughly 24 hours after landing from Los Angeles with a body clock still eight hours west — the pre-standby sleep is scheduled at what your body reads as early afternoon and will be short.
options: Ask crewing to move the standby window later in the day, or to swap it
Treat the 06:00–12:00Z sleep on 29 Sep as the real sleep and the evening block as a top-up
Blackout blinds, no caffeine after mid-afternoon on 29 Sep, and get bright morning light on 29 Sep to pull the clock east
If you're called out late in the window for a long duty, assess honestly against how much you actually slept and use the fatigue call if it isn't there

conflicts.statement: Between the 09-06 arrival (off duty 00:15Z on 7 Sep) and the 09-07 report at 20:40Z you get one daytime sleep at home between two transatlantic duties, with no night in your own bed at a normal hour.
options: Sleep as soon as you're through the door at about 01:10Z rather than winding down
Set no alarm before 09:00Z and clear the day of family or admin commitments
Ask crewing whether the 7 Sep sector can be swapped or given to reserve
File a fatigue report on the pairing construction regardless of the outcome
